description: Often described as the golden age of Hollywood, the studio era provided American filmmaking with unusual stability during a period (1930-60) that was everything but stable. We will consider the interrelations of Hollywood and American society and politics during the era, as well as the inner workings of the studios themselves and the particular form their product, the classical Hollywood cinema, took. Film genres include musicals, melodrama, war films, comedy, westerns, horror and sci-fi films.
